hints.content: To translate $\triangle ABC$ using $(x,y)\to(x ,y +3)$, we basically translate $\triangle ABC$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{C(-6,2)}$ is translated to $(-6 ,2 +3)=\greenD{(-6,5)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a triangle with vertices A B C and Vertex A at negative four, negative three, vertex B at zero, zero, and vertex C at negative six, two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves from vertex C three units up to a point at negative six, five.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a triangle with vertices A B C and Vertex A at negative four, negative three, vertex B at zero, zero, and vertex C at negative six, two. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves from the three vertices up three units to form the image of a congruent triangle with vertices at negative six, five, negative four, zero, and zero, three.
